from.place: Assertion (3), the phrase 'the abelian category whose objects are inverse systems in A and whose morphisms are compatible levelwise maps': that this category is abelian with levelwise kernels, cokernels and exactness, used in the Roos-complex comparison to compute the cokernel of the split envelope and the kernel of a degreewise epimorphism of complexes of towers

title: Inverse systems in an abelian category form an abelian category, computed levelwise
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ be the category of inverse systems $(T_n,f_n:T_{n+1}\to T_n)_{n\geq1}$ in $\mathcal A$ with morphisms of inverse systems [def-weil-inverse-system], with the levelwise addition of morphisms $(\varphi+\psi)_n=\varphi_n+\psi_n$. Then $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ is an abelian category, and for every $n\geq1$ the evaluation functor $\operatorname{ev}_n:\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal A$, $(T_m)_m\mapsto T_n$, is additive and exact: finite products, kernels and cokernels of $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ are computed levelwise (the kernel of $\varphi:T\to T'$ is the system $(\ker\varphi_n)_n$ with the induced transition maps, and similarly for cokernels). In particular a morphism $\varphi$ of inverse systems is a monomorphism, resp. an epimorphism, if and only if every $\varphi_n$ is one, and a sequence $0\to T\to T'\to T''\to0$ in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ is short exact if and only if $0\to T_n\to T'_n\to T''_n\to0$ is short exact in $\mathcal A$ for every $n$.

mathlib_match.how: one declaration per clause, with Tow(A) = the functor category (ℕ≥1)ᵒᵖ ⥤ A (equivalently ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A after reindexing): abelian by the instance functorCategoryAbelian (FunctorCategory.lean:96, read with sed); evaluation at n preserves finite limits and finite colimits by evaluation_preservesLimitsOfShape and evaluation_preservesColimitsOfShape (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/FunctorCategory/Basic.lean:225 and :319; an abelian category has finite limits and colimits), so kernels, cokernels and finite products are levelwise and ev_n is exact; mono and epi are levelwise by NatTrans.mono_iff_mono_app and NatTrans.epi_iff_epi_app (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Limits/FunctorCategory/EpiMono.lean:38 and :61; A has pullbacks and pushouts); the short-exactness clause follows, the comparison map from T to the levelwise kernel of T'→T'' being a levelwise isomorphism hence an isomorphism (NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app).
